title: Telehealth pilot — POC success plan and workshop notes
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the kickoff workshop notes, proposed deployment approach, and explicit success criteria for the TeleHealthCo pilot POC. Goal of the POC: validate that Redwood Inference can power a low-latency clinical-autocomplete and note-summarization flow integrated into TeleHealthCo’s EMR mock instance while meeting cost and safety constraints for a 6-week pilot.

Attendees (workshop on 2025-02-14): Maya Chen (SE lead), Rafael Ortega (Solutions Eng), Priya Nair (Product PM), Samantha Liu (TeleHealthCo eng lead), Dr. Aaron Stone (TeleHealthCo clinical SME), Jackson Park (Security), Clara Wu (Customer Success).

Scope (agreed):
- Features to prototype: clinical autocomplete (physician-facing), visit summary generation (discrete structured sections), and a short clinical-coding suggestion helper.
- Integration model: server-side API calls from a staging EMR instance (no PHI in POC; synthetic/ de-identified data only).
- Performance target environment: p3-equivalent or q4 quantized model on Dedicated pool.
- Timebox: 6 weeks (2 weeks integration + 3 weeks eval/run + 1 week wrap + handoff).

Success criteria (must be measurable):
1) Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end response time <= 750ms for autocomplete tokens under clinical workload (avg seq length 60).
2) Accuracy / clinical fidelity: 80% of clinician-supplied evaluation prompts rated acceptable by clinical SME (binary acceptable/not) across a 150-prompt validation set.
3) Hallucination ceiling: hallucination incidents <= 2% on the validation set (defined as generated explicit false statements about patient facts).
4) Cost: projected hosted cost per patient encounter inference <= $0.10 (token-normalized, including caching benefits) under expected volume of 2k encounters/day.
5) Reliability: system succeeds (no 5xx) for >= 99.5% of requests during 48-hour simulated traffic run at 2x expected load.
6) Security & compliance gating: data-in-transit encrypted end-to-end, no PHI stored in logs during POC; review and sign-off by TeleHealthCo security lead.
7) Ops handoff: deployment runbook and 1-hour training session scheduled with TeleHealthCo SREs.
8) Business acceptance: TeleHealthCo clinical product owner provides written sign-off that the POC met clinical utility bar.

Deployment proposal (recommended):
- Mode: Redwood Dedicated pool for the pilot window to guarantee throughput and consistent latency. If TeleHealthCo prefers VPC, propose Redwood Private evaluation (longer lead time).
- Model selection: start with a med-sized open clinical-tuned model (quantized int8) that is on the Redwood model catalog. If quality unacceptable, iterate to a higher-capacity variant.
- Autoscaling policy: conservative baseline pods sized for 200 concurrent short sessions, burst scaling for spikes to 500 sessions. Continuous batching with 200ms max latency budget.
- Caching: prefix-caching for repeated templates (e.g., standard patient history phrases) and KV cache for session continuations.
- Observability: enable per-route latency and token cost, add a custom tracing span for EMR->Redwood call chain, surface hallucination alerts to Slack #telehealth-poc.

Workshop decisions made / open questions: 
- Decided: Use dedicated pool for pilot.
- Decided: Synthetic PHI-only for POC; production PHI workflows will require Private deployment + KMS integration.
- Open: Which exact clinical model variant to start with — SE team to A/B test v1 (med-quant-int8) and v2 (large-int8) on week 1.
- Open: Escalation policy for clinician-reported hallucination incidents — propose webhook to TeleHealthCo incident system; need TeleHealthCo input.
- Open: Data retention policy for logs during POC; Jackson to provide recommended retention TTL and redaction rules by 2025-02-18.

Workshop notes (raw):
- Dr. Stone emphasized the importance of conservative language and explicit uncertainty phrases in suggestions. He asked for a toggle to disable suggestions in high-risk note sections.
- TeleHealthCo engineering wants minimal EMR-side changes: prefer a thin adapter that calls Redwood and receives JSON blocks (title, bullet list, confidence score).
- Priya requested we capture sample token counts per action to refine cost projection.
- Samantha requested a short latency demo within 48 hours after initial model spin-up.

Validation & evaluation plan:
- Week 0–1: Integration + smoke tests. Create a 150-prompt clinical validation set with TeleHealthCo SMEs; seed with edge cases.
- Week 2–4: Controlled clinician trials (n=12 clinicians), collect acceptability labels and incident reports. Automated logs for latency/5xx and hallucination heuristics.
- Week 5: 48-hour stress run at 2x expected traffic to validate reliability SLO.
- Week 6: Final analysis, cost projection, and business sign-off meeting.

Acceptance criteria checklist (for SE to present):
- [ ] Integration adapter deployed to staging EMR and calling Redwood endpoints.
- [ ] 95p latency <= 750ms in staging under representative load.
- [ ] Clinical acceptability >= 80% on the validation set.
- [ ] Hallucination incidents <= 2% and all incidents have reproducible examples logged.
- [ ] TeleHealthCo security sign-off on no PHI in logs and transport encryption validated.
- [ ] Ops runbook + training scheduled.

Risks and mitigation: 
- Model hallucinations: add conservative prompt engineering, uncertainty tokens, and a post-filter that blocks statements referencing non-existent patient facts.
- Unexpected cost: monitor token burn and enable quantized variants / caching if cost exceeds projection.
- Integration slippage: prioritize a minimal adapter with stubbed UI to validate end-to-end quickly.

Action items (owner — due):
- SE: spin-up two candidate model variants and run synthetic latency tests (Maya) — due 2025-02-17.
- Security: provide log retention and redaction TTL recommendations (Jackson) — due 2025-02-18.
- TeleHealthCo: provide clinician validation set seed and 3 SME volunteers (Samantha / Dr. Stone) — due 2025-02-16.
- Product: prepare cost projection spreadsheet with token estimates (Priya) — due 2025-02-19.
- SE: create runbook stub and schedule 1hr handoff (Maya) — due 2025-02-28.

Notes to self / SE reminders: 
- Keep a reproducible prompt/temperature config saved in repo — link will be added to linked_artifacts after PR.
- Demo checklist: quick latency demo, short usability screenshots, and 3 clinician quotes.

Proposed timeline (high level):
- Week A (integration): 2025-02-15 to 2025-02-21
- Week B (pilot run 1): 2025-02-22 to 2025-03-07
- Week C (validation + stress): 2025-03-08 to 2025-03-14
- Wrap + sign-off week: 2025-03-15 to 2025-03-21

Contact & escalation:
- SE lead: Maya Chen — maya.chen@redwood.ai, #se-telehealth in Slack
- TeleHealthCo PO: Priya Nair — priya.nair@telehealthco.com

Appendix (quick references):
- Minimum telemetry fields: request_id, route, model_variant, token_count, latency_ms, response_hash, hallucination_flag, clinician_label.
- Suggested model config template: max_tokens 512, temp 0.0–0.2 for autocomplete, top_p 0.95, stop_tokens ["
"].

End of doc.
